page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It has no local storage or bundled GPUs, but it supports Premium Storage for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-threaded performance and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top-tier results in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, and Redis SET operations also rank in the top 10% of tested systems. Furthermore, the Intel Xeon processor's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 capabilities contribute to strong performance in LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing with large 70B models. Single-core performance, however, sits in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D128s_v6 offers high resource density for highly parallelized workloads, delivering exceptional throughput per allocated virtual core. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means users must factor in the additional cost and latency of external Premium Storage. The absence of a dedicated GPU also limits its suitability for heavy real-time graphics rendering or deep learning training, though its CPU-based matrix extensions provide a viable alternative for moderate inference tasks.

This server type is highly suited for large-scale database operations, multi-threaded data processing, high-throughput static web serving, and software compilation. It is also well-positioned for CPU-bound machine learning inference and enterprise-grade general-purpose applications that require massive parallel processing capabilities without requiring local scratch disks.
